// what this is: The guard's configuration for the synthetic lab workload — the stand-in for a client's application.
Nothing here is recognised by name: the guard knows MetricIndex.LatencyP95Ms, the cluster exports
labapp_request_duration_seconds, and this file is the only thing that connects them. That is the point.
CpuThrottleRatio comes from cadvisor rather than the app, and is unbound here because no pod carries
a CPU limit. OomEventsRate comes from kube-state-metrics; see its own comment for why not cadvisor.
app's own error counter over its request counter, which the map cannot express as a single source, so it
is left out and reported blind.

It was bound anyway in the ConfigMap the same day, and the parity test later copied that binding into this file; removed 2026-08-10 (AN-D12). A parity gate makes two artefacts agree and has no opinion about which one was right.

OomEventsRate.query: sum by (pod) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{%selector%}[2m]) * on (namespace, pod, container) group_left() kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{%selector%,reason="OOMKilled"}) or sum by (pod) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{%selector%}[2m]) * 0)
_comment: NOT container_oom_events_total. Measured 2026-08-08 against a pod Kubernetes reported as OOMKilled
with exit 137: that series read 0 for the killed pod, and across 43 series cluster-wide over an hour
the only distinct value present was 0.0 - cAdvisor does not populate it on this runtime. The channel
bound, reported a number, satisfied every coverage check and could never fire.
kube-state-metrics carries the fact in two series: the restart increase says an event happened inside
the window, the last-terminated reason says it was an OOM. A name and a kind cannot express a join,
which is why 'query' exists. Verbatim queries carry their own range - keep [2m] in step with
prometheus rate window by hand.
Bound 2026-08-09. It was absent from the metrics block, so the guard issued no query and counted
the channel blind in every cycle — 1 of 1, unchanged for the whole run.
The series only exist because the workload now carries a CPU limit: CFS accounting is created by a
quota, so without one there is nothing to read and no amount of binding would help.
1000m, not 200m, because SustainedThresholdOptions.ForCpuThrottling was calibrated on a pod limited
to one core, and a threshold describes the regime it was measured in.
Measured healthy at 1000m: per-pod share of a 20-minute window at or above the 5% threshold is
14.6-19.0%, against the rule's 25% - so the healthy population is quiet with margin on both sides.
CORRECTED 2026-08-09. The first binding set kind=Ratio and nothing else, and MetricMap.Build renders
Ratio as `{name}{selector}` — no rate(), no division. The channel therefore queried the raw cumulative
counter, which only ever rises, and the trend family reported it in every window: 12 findings across a
replay window where the true ratio was 0.0000 on all twelve pods. A config entry overrode a correct
built-in template with a broken one.
Deleting the entry is not the fix: an unbound channel is issued no query and counts blind. The verbatim
query below is what PromqlCatalog would have built.
ActiveRequests closes the hung-request gap: a request only enters the duration histogram when it
FINISHES, so while one hangs every latency percentile stays quiet. Measured 2026-08-09 with five
requests deliberately hung: labapp_active_requests read 6 while the histogram count read 0.
The exporter subtracts the scrape itself, so 0 means idle. Before that subtraction every pod
reported a flat 1.0 and the observer dominated the signal.
Floors from measurement: at rest 0 on all twelve pods, ten-minute maxima 0/1/2.
Closes a gap every current channel is structurally blind to: contention produces a latency cliff
with NORMAL CPU and NORMAL GC, because a thread waiting on a monitor is not running.
Measured 2026-08-09 with the contended lock ON THE REQUEST PATH: p50 47 -> 1210 ms, p95 63 -> 5837 ms,
throughput 759 -> 26 requests per 10 s, contention rate 2 -> 12/s. Clearing the fault returned every
number to its starting value.
The instrument is OBSERVABLE, so it reports nothing until polled - before RecordObservableInstruments
was called it read a clean, well-formed, permanent zero through sixteen contending threads.
Floor RECALIBRATED 2026-08-09. The first value, 0.064, came from a peak of 0.0514 measured over only
~3 minutes on pods that had just started, and it produced a false positive on an unfaulted pod within
the hour. Re-measured over a settled 20-minute window across both pod generations: healthy per-pod peak
0.0952/s, so healthy replicas routinely exceeded the old floor. 0.0952 x 1.25 = 0.119, which is still
about 97x below the injected fault at 11.6/s.
The lesson is the window, not the number: a floor calibrated on three minutes of a freshly rolled
population describes the rollout, not the workload.
First-chance exceptions. Distinct from ErrorRate, which counts 5xx RESPONSES: an exception that is
caught and retried never becomes a 5xx, so the error rate stays flat while the process is already
failing.
Measured 2026-08-09 with half of requests throwing-and-catching: exceptions 0 -> 40/s while the 5xx
rate stayed at 0, p95 went 63.2 -> 63.1 -> 63.2 ms, throughput was unchanged and NOT ONE response
was other than 200. This is the one of the three runtime channels where every existing channel is
genuinely blind - unlike lock contention, where CPU also moved.
Healthy is exactly 0 on all twelve pods, so InertChannels() will report it as constant-zero and
AMBIGUOUS. That is correct: it is what a working rare-event channel looks like when the rare event
has not happened.
CPU pressure (PSI): time tasks spent waiting for CPU, from the kernel, per cgroup.
It measures DENIAL rather than usage, and unlike CpuThrottleRatio it needs no CPU quota to exist -
which is why it covers starvation on clusters that set no limits.
Measured 2026-08-09 on 12 pods, healthy then with one pod starved (~2 cores of demand against a
1-core quota): healthy max 0.00003, starved max 0.48682 - a separation of 16485x, the sharpest of
any channel in this system. Peers stayed under 0.00005 throughout.
waiting, not stalled: both were measured side by side and read 0.48682 vs 0.48681 under starvation.
For a single-container cgroup 'some task delayed' and 'all tasks delayed' are the same event, so
binding both would duplicate one signal.
Floor 0.00004 = healthy max x 1.25, about 12000x below the fault. No absolute rule yet - that is
PS-3, which needs its own calibration.
Absolute rule armed 2026-08-09 (PS-3). Threshold 0.01 = 1% of time with a task waiting on CPU,
held for a quarter of the window.
Measured, both sides: healthy peak across twelve pods 0.00005, starved MINIMUM sample 0.167 - the
threshold is 200x above the first and 16x below the second. Three orders of magnitude of empty space
between health and fault, which is why the exact value inside it is not load-bearing.
Breach fraction 0.25 follows ForCpuThrottling's measured shape: persistence separates a starved pod
from a busy one, not height.
AN-D9. The fraction of scrape attempts that succeeded, per pod, over the trailing 15 minutes.
Closes the PARTIAL-reporting gap: RunSilentPods already catches a pod that reports nothing at all,
but one successful sample resets its counter, so a pod answering some scrapes and missing others
keeps full membership in the window and has its incomplete series used as if complete.
SOURCE, and this is the part that is not interchangeable. The five container-level channels come
from kubelet/cAdvisor - a different scrape target from the app's own /metrics, which is the one that
saturates (RS-6). Coverage computed from any of them would read 100% throughout the fault. Prometheus
writes `up` on every scrape ATTEMPT regardless of outcome, so it is the only series that can answer.
WHY A VERBATIM QUERY. kind=Ratio renders `name{selector}` - the raw 0/1 gauge. Measured against the
detector: the peer comparison's size gate reads each pod's MEDIAN, and the median of a 0/1 series is
1.0 for any pod above 50% coverage, so a pod at 65% is indistinguishable from a healthy one. Only a
value that is already a fraction moves the median. avg_over_time is what produces one.
RANGE 15m = AnomalyGuardOptions.RecentWindow, not a new number. At the lab's measured 15 s scrape
interval (count_over_time(up[1m]) = 4 on all 12 pods, 2026-08-10) that is 60 attempts per value.
NO minGap, and its absence is a decision rather than an omission. MinAbsoluteGap exists because the
relative gate cannot say 'fourteen percent of nothing is nothing' - it divides by the signal's
magnitude. Here the magnitude is exactly 1.0 by construction, so the 8% relative gate IS the absolute
one: 8% of coverage, about 5 missed scrapes in 15 minutes. An absolute floor above ordinary noise
still needs a faulted arm to measure and none has been run; adding a guessed one would be a
threshold with a measurement's authority on a gate whose failure mode is silence.
calibrated:false is REQUIRED, not tidiness. Healthy coverage is a constant 1.0, so every folded peer
gap is |1.0-1.0| = 0 and FloorCalibrator would propose exactly 0.0 while healthy - and 1.25x the
first real fault once it has seen one, permanently raising the bar against the event the channel
exists for. It also stops InertChannels() reporting a WORKING channel as a confirmed dead binding:
Min == Max == 1.0 and InertChannel.IsConclusive tests Value != 0.0 unconditionally. That arrives
after 240 observations, which is one per pod per window - twenty cycles, about 100 minutes at 12
replicas and a 5-minute cadence.
requirePersistence:true because a pod being replaced stops answering for a moment on every rollout,
and a rollout replaces all of them. The count is silentPodCycles, not a second knob.
PRECONDITION for any other cluster: this assumes exactly one `up` series per pod. A service mesh
sidecar or a second scrape target against the same pods produces more, and the selector then needs
job="..." added explicitly. Verified on this lab 2026-08-10: 12 pods, 12 series, job=lab-workload.
